chain.note: Both trees follow the paper's route (exchange network, frames, labels, s<Wm, tau, interchange and layer recurrences, synthetic transforms and convolution, resampling and chirp, algorithm, time bound). A carries the central saving link by link with its mechanisms and constants: the bank-exchange proof, the telescoping budget Wm-2N+2L, the deficits N-2L_b and 2N-2L_c, eta_b and eta_c, the m^{1-2^{-50}} > m(1-eta) step, and the Phi_{I_m} frame identity that makes the bit network apply H<-H+D on every row. B reaches the same nodes but thins out at the bank exchange, the complex interface (statement only) and the exact deficits.

errors.says: A route from role w to rho(w) applies D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1} to its array (and S2.4.2 says the network applies only D_out D_in^{-1}).
errors.paper: For a signed role permutation the route applies epsilon_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1}; the sign matters for the complex network, whose Y->X route has sign -1.

errors.says: After the Harvey-van der Hoeven O(n log n) bound, a further saving must beat a logarithmic factor by a power.
errors.paper: The paper says only that it obtains a strict power saving in the logarithmic factor; it does not claim that any further saving must be a power saving.

overall.reason: Neither plan has a major error; B has two minor misstatements (the dropped route sign and an over-read of the introduction). On the core items A carries essential derivation steps that B states only as results: the bank-exchange mechanism (B1-B3), the complex phase mechanism (P1, P2, P4), the label budget (L2-L4), the matrix-shear factorization and specialization (M1-M3), the guard-width argument (S1-S3, S5), and the frame identity giving H<-H+D on every row, plus the exact deficits eta_b and eta_c. B has nothing of substance that A lacks.
